newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche new heart drug gets FDA approval.
newsitem.headline: Roche new heart drug gets FDA approval.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals giant Roche Holding AG said its cardiovascular drug Mibefradil, known under the trademarked name Posicor, has been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
Posicor is designed to treat hypertension and angina pectoris. It is the first selective T-calcium-channel blocker and can be given once daily for both indications, Roche said in a statement.
Analysts are optimistic about the prospects for Posicor, one of three new drugs which Roche is gearing up to launch this year.
The other two are an obesity drug called Xenical and Tasmar for the treatment of Parkinson's disease.
Posicor has already been approved for the treatment of hypertension and angina pectoris in Switzerland, the Netherlands and several countries in Latin America and Asia.
The drug is proceeding as planned in Europe following the European mutual recognition procedure, Roche also said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
